gates.requirement: RoomSceneComposerTests.cs and RoomSceneContractTests.cs each declare part of the single Edit Mode fixture NoSafeCircle.DoorPrototype.Tests.Editor.World.RoomSceneCompositionFoundationTests, a partial class; those file names are not type names. That one fixture verifies catalog completeness/order, root and anchor contracts, source-scene immutability, local-reference ownership, build-settings exclusion, and composition failure before canonical save. Sorting is deliberately not among the clauses this gate proves. The project defines exactly one sorting layer, Default, and DoorPrototypeSceneBuilder.WorldSpriteSortingLayerName is that same layer, so RoomSceneComposer.ValidateSortingConvention cannot fail: Unity refuses every attempt to move a renderer off Default when no other layer exists, including assigning sortingLayerID directly (probed in Unity at 7a1bae97a). The guard stays in the code for the day a dedicated layer exists, and this gate claims only what it can prove today.

gates.notes: Verified from the committed tree at the validated commit. Assets/NoSafeCircle/DoorPrototype/Generated/World/RoomSceneCatalog.asset and its .meta are both committed, and the meta carries a stable GUID e29ec0c6941d9dc489d1560b67557c92 under NativeFormatImporter rather than a GUID-only stub. The catalog records exactly the five stable room scene paths in fixed order: RuinedEntry, BoneArchive, ChapelOfAsh, LowerVault, FinalRoom under Assets/Scenes/Rooms/. The fixture asserts the order and the distinct stable paths (CanonicalRooms_MatchFixedFiveRoomOrder, CanonicalRooms_RecordDistinctStableScenePaths). Per-room asset creation and identity belong to NSC-044 through NSC-048, which this gate defers to.
gates.requirement: The shared catalog asset and every shared generated code/data asset carry deterministic Unity .meta identities. The catalog records the five stable room scene paths, while NSC-044 through NSC-048 own creation and identity of each room-specific asset.

gates.notes: Two consecutive foundation builds were run at the validated commit and compared semantically, because a rebuild is never byte-identical: recreated objects receive fresh random fileIDs. Both builds produced 1261 objects across 66 distinct (class, script) keys with no count differences and no size differences, and a component/value snapshot of the generated-root hierarchy after each build was identical. No duplicates appeared. The checkout was restored afterwards and reported 0 changes. The fixture proves the composer-level half separately: TryComposeRoom_RunTwice_ReplacesComposedRoomWithoutDuplicating and TryComposeRoom_ValidSourceScene_ClonesContentAndClosesSourceWithoutSaving.
gates.requirement: Two consecutive foundation builds produce the same global generated-root hierarchy, component values, catalog, and object counts without duplicates; composer tests using isolated fixtures prove deterministic input handling without creating or rewriting the five room assets.

gates.notes: Build-settings exclusion is proven by the fixture: AreRoomScenesExcludedFromBuild_CatalogRoomPaths_AreNotRegisteredInBuildSettings. On scene load/unload APIs the honest statement is narrower than "none exist": production code contains exactly one call, Scripts/DemoRunFlow.cs:296, SceneManager.LoadScene(SceneManager.GetActiveScene().buildIndex), reachable only from the "Press R to play again" end-screen handler. It reloads the active scene by its own build index, which is a run restart, not a room transition, so the gate's requirement - that no room-transition code calls scene load/unload APIs - holds. Playability is covered by VAL-005. Final content composition remains deferred to NSC-049.
gates.requirement: Automated checks prove Assets/Scenes/DoorPrototype.unity remains the only enabled gameplay scene, no production room-transition code calls scene load/unload APIs, and the existing canonical prototype remains playable while final content composition is deferred to NSC-049.
